review_subject: FRANK/ClayCode assumption that computational expressibility remains separate from external effect/resource authority and that typed host adapters should be preferred over new domain syntax when sufficient

independent_inputs.source: WebAssembly Component Model MVP handle/resource semantics
independent_inputs.finding: own/borrow handles are opaque, table-mediated, type-classified and dynamically lifetime-checked
resources are abstract lifetime-bearing entities passed indirectly by handles; own and borrow differ semantically
20,000 randomized operations matched an independent oracle; removing freshness, borrow-close or type checks created concrete counterexamples

counterhypotheses_tested: opaque handle identity alone is enough
borrow tracking can be omitted dynamically without replacement proof
resource type identity can be erased safely
refinement: The external authority boundary is supported for this slice, but the strongest evidence supports a backend-neutral typed ResourceHandle/FFI lowering contract with explicit lifetime/freshness/type rules rather than new DB-specific ClayCode syntax. Capability epoch and resource lifetime epoch must remain conceptually separable until target evidence shows when they should couple.
not_supported: claim that runtime checks must duplicate guarantees already proven by a target backend
next_falsifier: Compile the same frozen resource contract to the selected Ubuntu-native and/or WASM/WASI backend, then differential-test generativity, stale/ABA reuse, own/borrow transfer, cancellation/drop and capability revocation with target receipts.
